verdictReason: Killed on three major reasons: (1) ExitBid's primary page confirms a flat $199 with 0% commission (4% of a $5K sale), under the entrant's 5% = $250, triggering the scan-1 falsifier; (2) escrow and niche focus are not edges, since directories already have categories on Flippa (1.9M+ claimed buyers) and Microns and escrow is already provided; (3) ~$200 per deal at thin volume gives ~$700 base profit (~$1/owner-hour) and about -$710 pessimistic.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: ExitBid: flat $199, 0% commission, Escrow.com (D1, D3). Vertos: free listing plus 5%, vendor claim only (E6; primary page not fetchable). Flippa: $29 flat entry listing plus 10%, with a Directory category (D7, D9, D6). Microns: Directory Websites for Sale category from about $1,200 (D8). Acquire.com: 8% plus $25/month, free escrow (D4, D5), though a homepage testimonial says sellers pay nothing (D11). Free DIY posting on communities is plausible but I did not read any page on it (unverified). None is a directory-only marketplace, so coverage of the wedge is partial, but all cover price and escrow.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists, and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None. Price is already matched or beaten (D1), escrow is a commodity used by rivals (D3, D5), and niche focus is copyable: Flippa and Microns already expose directory categories (D6, D8) and could add a directory landing page overnight. The only compounding asset would be a directory-specific buyer list, which the entrant starts at zero against Flippa's claimed 1.9M buyers (D6). Falsifier: evidence of a sizeable group of sub-$10K directory buyers or sellers that these platforms demonstrably fail to serve, e.g. listings that expire unsold in the directory category; I found none.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Sellers pay Flippa a $29 listing fee plus 10% (about $529 on a $5,000 sale) (D7, D9); Acquire.com sellers pay 8% plus $25/month (D4); ExitBid sellers pay $199 flat (D1); Acquire buyers pay subscriptions from $390 (old E4; Acquire pricing page lists Buyer membership from $390). So sellers do pay, but the lowest verified rate is $199 on a flat basis. No page I read shows how many sub-$10K directories actually sell or any deal count for the directory category.

answers.question: (4) Legal/platform constraints?
answers.answer: Using Escrow.com (as ExitBid and Acquire.com do, D3, D5) avoids holding funds; Flippa lists Escrow.com from 1.2% (D7). I could not read Escrow.com's marketplace/partner terms (fetch refused), so whether a new marketplace can use it with an own fee layer is unverified. Buyer-side fraud and fake revenue claims need a verification process (not researched). Consumer-protection/money-transmission treatment depends on never touching funds.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers (reference entrant: $1,000, 12 h/week, first revenue by day 90)?
answers.answer: Assumptions: fee 5% of an average $4,000 sale = $200 per deal (the Microns/ExitBid listings start around $1,000-$1,200, D8, so $4,000 is a guess); 8 closed deals between months 4 and 12 (assumption; incumbents show 14 live listings and 6 recent sales, D2, D8); costs $900 (site $150, legal $250, outreach $300, tools $200; assumptions; escrow fees paid by the parties). Base: revenue $1,600, profit ~$700 over ~620 owner hours (~$1/hour). Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): revenue $640, cost $1,350, profit ~-$710. To undercut ExitBid the fee must stay below $199, which caps revenue per deal.

newAlternatives.label: ExitBid: flat $199 per listing, 0% commission, Escrow.com available (one-off fee, not monthly)
Flippa: $29 flat entry listing for assets under $10K plus 10% commission (about $529 on a $5,000 sale); has a Directory category
Acquire.com: 8% closing fee below $250k plus $25/month listing; free escrow; buyers pay a subscription from $390
Microns: has Directory Websites for Sale category, asks from about $1,200 (seller fees not stated on the page read; cost 0 is a placeholder)
Vertos: free listing, flat 5% on sale (vendor claim only; primary page fetch refused)

killReasons.reason: The price edge is already taken: ExitBid charges a flat $199 with 0% commission (primary page), 4% of a $5,000 sale, which is below the entrant's 5% = $250; Vertos also claims free listing + flat 5% (vendor claim, old E6, primary page could not be fetched). Scan-1's own falsifier (rivals already at roughly $0-$250) is met, and price alone is not an edge.

The only differentiators left are niche focus and a third-party escrow, neither exclusive: escrow is already used or paid for by ExitBid and Acquire.com (D3, D5), and directories already have a dedicated category on Microns and on Flippa, which holds a claimed 1.9M+ buyer pool (D6, D8). A zero-audience entrant has no buyer pool and no way to assemble one cheaper than these incumbents.

Revenue ceiling is tiny: a 5% fee on a ~$4,000 average sub-$10K sale is ~$200 per deal, and visible deal flow in this segment is small (ExitBid shows 14 live listings at a time, Microns shows 6 recently sold; D2, D8) with sub-$10K assets the thin end of the market (D10). A pessimistic year-1 model loses money (~-$710) and the base case earns about $1 per owner hour.

Seller-side competitor pricing is itself disputed (Acquire.com testimonial says sellers pay nothing; pricing page shows 8% + $25/month), so the scan-1 $529 vs $250 comparison rests on unreliable inputs; this does not rescue the idea since ExitBid's $199 is confirmed.

assumptions: Fee 5% of an average $4,000 sale = $200 per closed deal (average sale price is an assumption; scan-1 used $5,000 = $250).
8 closed deals in year 1, none before month 4 (assumption; no source for deal volume in the directory category).
Costs $900: site/hosting $150, legal terms $250, outreach/marketing $300, tools $200 (assumptions); escrow fees paid by buyer/seller, not the entrant.
Pessimistic: fee x0.8 ($160), deals x0.5 (4), cost x1.5 ($1,350): revenue $640, profit -$710.
Owner hours 12/week for 52 weeks = 624 hours; base profit $700 is about $1.1 per hour.
